title: Void Ending in a Sextile to Venus
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The sextile is one of the two friendly aspects. Picatrix ties the Moon to the fortunes by trine and sextile whenever a work is meant to prosper, and grades the sextile as the aspect of moderate friendship: the signs it joins are kin in action but not in passion, so the concord between them is a lukewarm one.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a sextile to Venus, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of her sweetness and her song. Venus governs taste, the text says, and with it beauty and love: poetic meter, songs, dancing, painting, and perfumes fall to her, with places of music and merriment among her locations. She is the Lesser Fortune, and her benevolence fits the works of youths, pleasures, and women. Pearls are her stones, the sweet smells are hers, and her colors are sky blue and gold fading into green.
